name: English

_purpose.*_file: file names teamcall writes into the company's folder; the person sees them in their file list, so plain words in their language; {who} and {name} stay as they are
_purpose.charter_*: the pilot charter, read by the manager who sponsors the pilot
_purpose.fast_*: the 20-minute fast path card, read by one employee who has never used a terminal
_purpose.ch_*: the 5-hour champion path, read by the employee who will help colleagues
_purpose.boost_*: termboost: the same task once in the app and once in the terminal, then again with one command
_purpose.report_*: the pilot report for the company; it never names a person, only P1, P2, ...
_purpose.decide_*: a one-page decision for the manager: scale, fix and repeat, or stop
_purpose.rule_*: a per-program rule, said in one short line when that program is listed
_purpose.note_*: one line about how this computer's Claude Code is signed in
_purpose.card_*: one daily card read on a phone in half a minute: _title is a few words, _text says what to do today in one or two sentences, _show is the exact words to type or the screen to look at (sent when the person presses Show me). It teaches leading an agent and approving its steps, not chatting. Claude Code's own words (plan mode, /permissions, Yes, and don't ask again, /remote-control) stay in English
_purpose.lesson_done: button titles under each card (lesson_done, lesson_show, lesson_skip) and under the WhatsApp note (lesson_open): at most 20 characters, WhatsApp's limit
_purpose.lesson_ack_*: the bot's short reply after a button press, at most 200 characters; warm and plain
_purpose.lesson_welcome: the first message after the person joins; it reassures, so tone outranks dictionary accuracy
_purpose.lesson_template: the WhatsApp template body Meta approves: a short note that the person's own card {n} (like 3/20) is ready, with the button lesson_open under it; no lesson text and no offer in it, so Meta files it as utility. Plain words
_purpose.lesson_sent: what `lesson send` prints for the champion: each chat gets its own next card, one a day
_purpose.lesson_webhook_*: what `lesson webhook` says to the champion: where Telegram brings the presses now; commands in backticks stay as they are
_purpose.lesson_template_mov*: one line for the champion when Meta moves the approved template to another category; {category} stays as Meta writes it (UTILITY, MARKETING)
_purpose.lesson_schedule_*: a comment line above a schedule line the champion pastes into cron or Task Scheduler
_purpose.report_lessons*: the report's part on the daily cards; never a name

kept: already there, left as it is: {path}
charter_promise: In 30 days {people} people of the company go from the usual chat to working with an agent in the terminal, and the company grows to {target} people through its own champions. For every person the journal keeps the attempt, the time to the first working result, the workflow actually built, the help it took and, when someone stopped, the reason.
charter_waves_how: Weeks 1-2: the first people take the fast path and the first champion takes the 5-hour path. Weeks 3-4: each champion brings in about {per} colleagues with the same fast path.
charter_goal_text: At least {goal} working results confirmed among the first {people} people.
charter_key_metric: The key number: minutes of human help per successful first result.
m_coverage_example: 40 files processed instead of a sample of 10
m_repeatable_example: the work runs every week with one command
m_capability_example: the employee built a working tool of their own for the first time
m_risk_example: which parts a person still reviews
charter_setup: How the pilot is set up (one page for IT)
setup_devices: Devices: the company's computers, or own laptops on the company's route (gatecall, step B2).
setup_accounts: Accounts: one seat per person (Claude Team, or the seat the company already pays for - see `teamcall agents`).
setup_data: Data: work files and training files of the pilot; red folders stay with a model on the computer (gatecall).
setup_folders: Folders: the pilot's folder; the agent works on a copy until the person has seen the list of changes (safecall).
setup_review: Review: a person reads every result before it leaves the team; a second opinion from another company's AI on the important ones (duocall).
setup_install: Install and remove: one command each (the fast path card); removing deletes the program and its settings.
setup_contact: Contact when something goes wrong: the sponsor and the champion.
setup_actions: Sending, buying and publishing outside the company stay with the person: the agent prepares, the person presses.
setup_retention: Keeping and deleting: the journal and the reports stay in the company's folder; pilot copies are deleted on day 30.
setup_red_from_policy: Red folders from the company policy:
setup_providers_from_policy: AI vendors the company policy allows:
gives_people: people who really work at a computer
gives_devices: approved devices, AI accounts, kinds of data and test tasks
gives_payer: who pays for the seats (billcall counts it)
gives_measure: the first and the last measurement
gives_case: the right to describe the case without names
charter_next: Next: `teamcall fast --person <name>` for each person, `teamcall champion --person <name>` for the champion, and `teamcall log add` after each step.
fast_task_default: a real task from this week's work
fast_install_how: Open the terminal and paste: `{install}`. Then open a new terminal window and type `claude --version`.
fast_sign_in: Sign in with the work seat
fast_sign_in_how: Type `claude` and sign in in the browser with the company's account (claude.ai). Signed in this way, the phone works as a remote later.
fast_first_task_how: In a copy of the work folder say: "first a plan, then do it" and give the task: {task}. Read the plan, say yes, look at the result.
fast_claudemd: CLAUDE.md: the rules the agent reads every time
fast_claudemd_how: Ask: "write a CLAUDE.md for this folder: who I am, what I do here, three rules". Short direct instructions, at most {max} lines (`teamcall claudemd CLAUDE.md` checks).
fast_repeat_how: Turn the task into a command of its own (`teamcall boost`), then run it again with `/` and its name.
fast_log: Done? The champion writes it down: `teamcall log add --person "{person}" --stage first_artifact`.
champion_intro: The champion helps about {per} colleagues through the fast path and knows where people get stuck.
ch_plan_mode_how: Plan mode (Shift+Tab), what the agent asks before acting, and the folder copy before changes.
ch_claudemd: The team's CLAUDE.md and shared settings
ch_claudemd_how: One CLAUDE.md per team folder under 100 lines; `.claude/settings.json` shared in the folder.
ch_skills: The company's own skills and plugin
ch_skills_how: Turn the three most repeated tasks into skills and a company plugin (firmcall).
ch_second_opinion_how: A different company's AI checks the important results (duocall, sidecall); `teamcall agents` shows what the company's seats already include.
ch_remote_how: Remote Control and cloud sessions for work on the road (pocketcall).
ch_unblock_how: Read the journal (`teamcall log show`): who stopped at which step and why; the most frequent blocker gets fixed for everyone.
ch_measure_how: Before and after on one real task per person (`teamcall measure`), then `teamcall report`.
boost_title: The same task in the app and in the terminal: {name}
boost_term_1: the same folder opens with the agent
boost_app_3: next week: write it all again
boost_schedule: Next time it is one command: `/{name}` inside Claude Code, or `claude -p "/{name}"` from a schedule.
boost_skill_body:
Do this task in the current folder, the same way as last time: {task}

First say the plan in two lines, then do it, then list what changed.
claudemd_too_long: CLAUDE.md has {n} lines; keep it to {max} short direct instructions - a long one is read worse.
report_no_names: People are P1, P2, ... - no names in this report.
report_key_metric: Minutes of human help per successful first result
decision_repeat: Fix the blockers and repeat with the same people
decide_why_scale: {succeeded} of {count} people reached a first working result, {champions} champion(s), {help} minutes of help per result (limit {max}).
decide_why_repeat: {succeeded} of {count} people reached a first working result, {champions} champion(s), {help} minutes of help per result (limit {max}): not yet 3 of every 5 with a champion within the limit.
decide_why_stop: No first working result among {count} people.
decide_next_scale: Each champion brings in about 8 colleagues with the fast path; the seats are counted with billcall before buying.
decide_next_repeat: Take the most frequent blocker from the report, fix it for everyone, and run the fast path again for those who stopped.
decide_next_stop: Read where each person stopped; try branch B (Cowork or the app's Code tab) with the same task, then measure again.
move_title: Moving people to the terminal in 30 days
move_intro: Fast path for everyone in 20 minutes, one champion per team, and for each program the seat that already pays for it.
move_w1: the first 5 people: fast path; the first champion starts the 5-hour path
move_w2: each person turns one weekly task into a command (`teamcall boost`); measurement before and after
move_w3: champions bring in the next wave; the most frequent blocker is fixed for everyone
move_w4: report and decision: scale or stop (`teamcall report`, `teamcall decide`)
move_programs: Programs, and what pays for them
agents_title: Terminal agents and the seats that already pay for them
rule_copy_only_prepaid: works on a cleaned copy, with a prepaid balance
rule_training_only: works in a training folder (it has no read-only switch)
rule_no_blanket_permission: gets permissions one by one, never one for everything
note_api_key: Claude Code here signs in with an API key: the phone remote and cloud sessions need the claude.ai sign-in of a seat.
note_base_url: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points away from Anthropic: the phone remote is off in this window.
note_traffic: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC or DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK is set: the phone remote is off.
note_signed_in: Claude Code here is signed in with a claude.ai account.
setup_lessons: Daily cards: on each working day one short card in Telegram or WhatsApp from the company's own bot - how to lead an agent and approve its steps; the employee installs nothing (`teamcall lesson`).
report_lessons_sum: {sent} card(s) went to {people} people: {done} done, {show} asked to be shown, {skip} skipped, {silent} with no answer.
report_lessons_none: no cards sent yet (`teamcall lesson send`)
lesson_ack_done: Counted: done. The next card comes on the next working day.
lesson_ack_skip: Counted: skipped. The next card comes on the next working day.
lesson_welcome: You are in. On each working day one short card comes here: how to lead an agent and approve its steps. Under each card: Done, Show me, Skip. {card} brings the card of the day, {stop} ends the cards.
lesson_bye: No more cards. {start} brings them back.
lesson_unknown_link: teamcall does not know this link, or it is already used. Ask your champion for a new one.
lesson_template: Your daily card {n} from the company's AI pilot is ready. Tap the button below to read it here.
lesson_invite: The link for {person}: one tap and the daily cards start. {link}
lesson_joined_phone: {person} is on the list: the next card goes to this WhatsApp number - a short note with a button that opens it.
lesson_sent: {channel}: {sent} card(s) sent, {had} had one today already, {finished} have all {total}, {failed} not delivered
lesson_sent_day: {channel}: card {n}/{total} - sent {sent}, already had it {had}, not delivered {failed}
lesson_waiting: {count} person(s) start on {date}, the pilot's first day.
lesson_not_now: {time} is outside the hours of the cards ({at}-{until}): nothing sent.
lesson_weekend: {date} is a weekend day: the cards go on working days.
lesson_not_joined: Invited, not joined yet: {people}. Send them their link again: `teamcall lesson invite --person <name>`.
lesson_nobody: Nobody has joined the cards yet: `teamcall lesson invite --person <name>`.
lesson_no_card: {date}: no card today; the cards come on the pilot's working days 1-{total}.
lesson_serving: WhatsApp answers: listening at {address}. In the Webhooks of the Meta app give this address over HTTPS and TEAMCALL_WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN.
lesson_serving_telegram: Telegram answers: listening at {address}; Telegram brings them to the HTTPS address given to `lesson webhook`.
lesson_webhook_on: telegram: the presses and messages now come to {url} the moment they are made - keep `teamcall lesson serve` running behind that address; `lesson webhook --off` hands them back to `lesson pull`.
lesson_webhook_off: telegram: the presses and messages come to `teamcall lesson pull` again.
lesson_template_review: {lang}: Meta filed the template as {category}. Ask for a review in WhatsApp Manager - Message templates - Business support - Template category updates - Request review, within 60 days: the note holds only the person's own card number, no lesson text and no offer.
lesson_template_moved: {lang}: Meta has filed the template {name} as {category}.
lesson_template_moving: {lang}: on {date} Meta files the template {name} as {category}.
lesson_schedule_env: The company's tokens go into {file}: one line TEAMCALL_...=value each, readable only by you; teamcall reads it on every run.
lesson_schedule_launcher: Each line runs {file}: it finds the teamcall installed now, so an update of the plugin changes nothing here; what each run says goes into {log}.
lesson_schedule_windows: Paste the lines into PowerShell as yourself: the tasks run without a window, on battery too, and a run missed while the computer was off comes when it is on again.
lesson_schedule_card: Every working day from {at} to {until}, every 15 minutes while this computer is on: each person's next card, one a day
lesson_schedule_answers: The Telegram buttons and "Show me": one receiver that stays on; every 5 minutes it starts again if it stopped
lesson_schedule_serve: WhatsApp: the receiver of the buttons, kept running the same way
lesson_schedule_mac: macOS: if the folder is in Desktop, Documents or Downloads, give /usr/sbin/cron Full Disk Access (System Settings - Privacy & Security).
card_1_text: Today give the agent a result to make, not a question to answer: what to make, from which files, where to put it. A chat answers; an agent does the work.
card_1_show: Instead of "how do I add up these invoices?" type: "Add up the invoices in this folder by client into totals.csv. First a plan."
card_2_text: Ask for the plan before any change. Read it as a colleague's proposal: say yes, or say which step to change.
card_2_show: In Claude Code press Shift+Tab until the bottom line says plan mode, then give the task. The agent answers with numbered steps and waits. Type "yes", or "step 3: keep the old file".
card_3_title: Approve one step at a time
card_3_text: When the agent asks to run a command or change a file, read what exactly it will do. Say yes to this one step; keep "Yes, and don't ask again" for safe repeats.
card_3_show: The agent asks: "Run: rm old/*.tmp?" Read the command and the folder. Choose "Yes" for this time only. "Yes, and don't ask again" fits a check you run every day.
card_4_text: Before the first real task, copy the folder and start the agent in the copy. You compare the two and keep what you like.
card_4_show: Copy "Reports" to "Reports-try", open the terminal in "Reports-try" and type claude. When it is done, compare the two folders and move back the files you want.
card_5_text: Before you accept a result, ask the agent for the list of what it changed, and read it. That list is what you approve.
card_5_show: Type: "List every file you changed, one line on what changed in each." Open two of them and check. Then say "accepted" or "undo the change in totals.csv".
card_6_text: If the agent goes the wrong way, stop it at once and say what to do instead. Stopping is part of leading.
card_6_show: Press Esc: the agent stops. Type: "Leave the table as it was; fix only the dates in column B." It goes on from there.
card_7_text: Write three rules into CLAUDE.md in your folder: who you are, what you do here, what never to touch. The agent reads them at every start.
card_7_show: Type: "Write a CLAUDE.md: I prepare the monthly sales report; the sources are in data/; never change files in archive/." Keep it short: well under 100 lines.
card_8_text: Give the agent files and folders instead of pasted text: it reads the whole source, and you skip the copying.
card_8_show: Type @ and the start of a file name; Claude Code suggests the files. "Compare @data/march.csv with @data/april.csv and list what changed."
card_9_text: Ask the agent to check its result against the sources before it shows it to you. You approve a checked result.
card_9_show: Add to the task: "When done, check every total against the source files and show me the lines that differ."
card_10_title: One command for a weekly task
card_10_text: A task you do every week becomes one command: you approve how it works once, and next time you start it with one word.
card_10_show: Type: "Turn what we just did into a project skill named weekly-report." Next week type /weekly-report and read the plan it shows before you say yes.
card_11_text: Before you approve a plan, ask the agent what it assumed. A wrong assumption costs a minute before the work and an hour after it.
card_11_show: Type: "Before you start: your assumptions about this task, in three lines." Correct the wrong one: "No, our fiscal year starts in April."
card_12_text: Split a big task into steps and approve the result of each step before the next one. A small step is quick to check.
card_12_show: Type: "Do only step 1 of the plan, then stop and show me the result." Check it, then: "Good, step 2."
card_13_text: Give a lasting yes only to commands you know, one by one. Deleting, sending and installing keep asking you.
card_13_show: Type /permissions and add one allow rule for a command you run every day, for example Bash(python3 check_report.py). Nothing else changes: the rest still asks.
card_14_text: Sending, buying and publishing outside the company stay with you: the agent prepares, you read and press.
card_14_show: Type: "Prepare the email to the supplier as a draft file; do not send it." Read the draft, then send it yourself from your mail.
card_15_text: For an important result, let a fresh session review it before you approve. It sees the result without the path that led there.
card_15_show: Open a new terminal window, type claude and say: "Review totals.csv against the files in data/ and list any line that looks wrong. Change nothing."
card_16_text: A long task can run while you are away: its questions come to your phone, and you approve the steps there.
card_16_show: In Claude Code type /remote-control, then open the session in the Claude app on your phone. When the agent asks for a permission, read the question there and answer yes or no.
card_17_title: Pick up where you left off
card_17_text: Yesterday's work goes on: continue the same session, with its plan and its context, instead of starting over.
card_17_show: In the same folder type: claude --continue. Or type /resume inside Claude Code and pick yesterday's session from the list.
card_18_text: Time one real task before and after: how long by hand, how long with the agent, your checking included.
card_18_show: Write two numbers, for example "invoice report: 90 min by hand, 27 min with the agent, checking included", and give them to your champion.
card_19_title: Stuck? One line to the champion
card_19_text: More than ten minutes without moving on? Write one line to your champion: the step, what you typed, what happened.
card_19_show: "Step: the first task. I typed: add up the invoices. It asked to run python3 and I did not know whether to allow it." The champion answers, and fixes it for everyone.
card_20_text: Show one colleague, in ten minutes, a task you now do with the agent: the result you asked for, the plan, your yes, the result.
card_20_show: Sit together, open your folder, type the task with "first a plan", read the plan aloud, approve it and show the result. Then let your colleague type the next one.
